Vanessa,

Thanks for the materials so far. As we prepare the RFP response, procurement and engineering want a more detailed implementation playbook that covers:

- High-level timeline (milestones and gated checkpoints)
- Integration touch-points ( APIs, webhooks, expected data flows )
- Canary strategy: duration, traffic % targets, rollback gates
- Downtime/maintenance windows and expected customer work items
- Security/compliance prerequisites (SOC2 evidence items, key rotation, KMS)

Could you share a single consolidated document that includes a week-by-week timeline and a simple step-by-step integration checklist? Procurement would like to see the canary/rollback language explicitly called out so legal can review.

If you can send a draft by end of day Monday 11/15, that would help us stay on the RFP schedule.

Thanks — happy to set a quick call if that helps.

Hi Tamara — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a concise implementation overview that addresses each bullet (Attachment: aurora-implementation-overview.pdf). High level summary below:

- Proposed delivery: 8 weeks from kickoff to production canary; 4-week pilot then 4-week staged ramp.
- Integrations: REST-based ingestion endpoint + optional S3 batch for bulk onboarding; auth via mTLS or OAuth2 (customer choice).
- Canary: 2-week canary with progressive traffic slices (5% \u2192 25% \u2192 50%), automated health gates tied to error rates and latency SLOs.
- Rollback: automatic fallback to previous model variant + traffic stepdown; full cutback takes <15 minutes in tested scenarios.
- Data residency: US-only option available; audit logs retained 365 days by default (configurable).

Next steps I propose:
1) I'm copying our solutions engineer, Aditya Rao, and onboarding lead, Monica Patel, to estimate SE-days and to validate the canary gate thresholds.
2) We'll deliver a detailed week-by-week timeline + cutover checklist by Monday 11/15.
3) If procurement wants stricter SLAs on retention or a custom KMS/HSM integration, we'll mark that as an enterprise option in the SOW.

(Attachment: aurora-implementation-overview.pdf)

Would you prefer a 30-minute walkthrough on Monday afternoon or would written details suffice for now?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa / Monica — I reviewed Tamara's asks and the draft timeline. Key technical notes and recommended integration sequence below: 

1) Ingestion & auth
   - Primary path: REST API with OAuth2 client credentials (recommended for scale).
   - Optional: mTLS for highest-assurance customers; requires cert exchange step during pre-kickoff.

2) Data mapping & onboarding (Week 1-2)
   - Deliverables: schema mapping doc, sample file ingest, sandbox keys.

3) Pilot / 2-week canary (Week 3-4)
   - Traffic slices: 5% (48h) -> 25% (72h) -> 50% (7d).
   - Gates: error rate <0.5% 95th latency <600ms CPU/GPU error counters stable; quality checks on sample prompt/response set.

4) Staged ramp (Week 5-8)
   - Progressive scaling + cache warmup; monitor token-cost vs latency tradeoffs.

5) Rollback plan
   - Immediate rollback to previous model variant if gates fail; automated traffic stepdown + alerting + postmortem window.

Security & compliance
   - SOC2 artifacts: we can produce our SOC2 Type II summary and mapping document.
   - Audit log retention: default 365 days; we can extend to custom retention via SOW.

Operational needs (customer)
   - Provide: sandbox creds, sample payloads, maintenance window for final cutover (we recommend a 4-hour block).

Estimated SE effort: 10 SE-days (onboarding + pilot) + 6 SE-days for cutover support + 2 days for runbook and testing = 18 SE-days.

Attachment: integration-checklist.md

If you want, I can convert the gates into Prometheus query examples and a Grafana dashboard template.

— Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Consolidated: Aurora implementation & cutover playbook (draft)

Hi Tamara —

Thanks — attached is the consolidated cutover playbook (Attachment: aurora_cutover_playbook_v1.pdf) and a link to the editable drive folder where you'll find the timeline spreadsheet and gate definitions: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cAuroraCutoverDraft

Summary of proposed plan (dates are placeholders pending kickoff):
- Week 0 (prep): contract signed, PO issued, sandbox creds exchanged, certs (if mTLS)
- Weeks 1-2 (onboard): schema mapping, test ingest, smoke tests
- Weeks 3-4 (pilot/canary): 2-week canary: 5% -> 25% -> 50% as Aditya described; automated gates and manual review points on day 3 and day 10
- Weeks 5-8 (ramp): steady scaling to full production, cache warmups, full QA pass

Rollout gates and acceptance criteria (short):
- Service errors <0.5% over 24h window across endpoints
- 95th pct latency <600ms for production traffic
- No data residency violations (all traffic kept within US region)
- Quality:-prompt-level pass rate > 92% on sample set (we'll finalize test prompts with your team)

Customer responsibilities (pre-kickoff)
- Provision sandbox accounts and test payloads
- Schedule a 4-hour maintenance window for final cutover (we suggest Sat 02:00–06:00 PT)
- Confirm KMS/HSM requirements if needed

SE effort estimate: 18 SE-days (Aditya) + onboarding lead support (Monica) for documentation and runbook reviews.

Next steps we request from Aurora:
1) Confirm the maintenance window preference (Sat maintenance preferred)
2) Confirm desired auth method (OAuth2 vs mTLS)
3) Provide preferred DocuSign contact for SOW execution

If that looks good I'll update the SOW and send a DocuSign envelope for signature.

(Attachment: aurora_cutover_playbook_v1.pdf)

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
